extracted.intended_audience: media producers, broadcasters, podcast makers, journalists, and organizations considering submission to the Peabody Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how the Peabody Awards evaluate submissions for excellence in storytelling across electronic media, including high-level philosophy, procedural selection steps, category structure, and illustrative (implicit) newsworthiness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: No set criteria for judging the winners
rubrics_metrics.description: "There are no set criteria for judging the winners."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Peabody explicitly states it does not use a fixed checklist; judgments are not formulaic and are made case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories that illuminate social issues with depth and complexity as much as stories that entertain and inspire
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize "stories that illuminate social issues with depth and complexity as much as stories that entertain and inspire through their art or voice."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on both substantive civic/social illumination and artistic/expressive excellence; entries may be valued for either or both qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor 'stories that matter'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the overarching evaluative mindset: significance and impact are central to selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each entrant judged on its own merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entrant judged on its own merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons across different kinds of work are limited by evaluating each submission within its own qualities and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unanimous selection required
rubrics_metrics.description: Only unanimously selected programs receive a Peabody Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are granted only when the Board reaches full agreement, indicating a very high threshold for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual evaluation of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry evaluated on the achievement of standards established within its own context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgment takes into account the specific context, genre, format, production constraints, and intended audience of the entry rather than applying one universal standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening and intensive board meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Process: initial screening round → 3 intensive board meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selection process includes an initial triage of entries followed by multiple in-depth deliberations by the Board of Jurors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Board of Jurors
rubrics_metrics.description: Diverse Board of Jurors (top-level thought leaders from varied backgrounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's diversity of professional and cultural backgrounds is an explicit feature of the adjudication process and influences deliberation perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominee and winner quotas (typical volumes)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1300+ entries received annually; process yields ~60 nominees → ~30 winners per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a sense of competitiveness and scale; only a small fraction of submitted work reaches nominee/winner status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-based evaluation (eight categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight Categories: Entertainment; Documentary; Arts; Children's / Youth; News; Podcast / Radio; Interactive & Immersive; Public Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are organized by category, implying evaluation is sensitive to the conventions and aims of each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social significance / illumination of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Social significance / illumination of issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that sheds light on important public or social issues is prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and complexity over breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Depth and complexity over breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for nuanced, in-depth treatment of topics rather than superficial or overly broad coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic voice / craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Artistic voice / craftsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of storytelling technique, craft, and distinctive voice are central considerations alongside informational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to inspire or move audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Capacity to inspire or move audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional resonance and the ability to engage or motivate audiences are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse perspectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of varied voices and viewpoints contributes to the work's merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service value
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Public service value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that serves the public interest—informing, educating, or improving civic life—is particularly relevant (note the separate 'Public Service' category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: Originality of approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel, inventive, or distinctive methods of storytelling and reporting are rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cultural relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that resonates across cultures or addresses issues with cross-cultural import is emphasized.
